title: Why Aglianico del Taburno tastes the way it does

lede.text: Fine-grained soils over soft rock generally hold plenty of water in these hills. Aglianico grown here makes dry, full-bodied ruby reds that turn garnet with age.

chapters.title: Hills around Benevento
paras: The vineyards lie in the province of Benevento, in Campania. They cover the whole of 9 municipalities and part of 4 more. Hills alternate with flat-bottomed karst hollows. Gullies cut between them record violent bouts of erosion in the Quaternary.

The zone is hilly overall, between 200 and 650 m above sea level. Only hillside and foothill vineyards count. Valley floors and damp ground are excluded. Across the province as a whole, vineyards sit from about 50 m up to about 500 m, depending on grape and ripening time.

fly.label: The Calore river
fly.caption: The zone's boundary follows the Calore river for about 2 km before it meets the Benevento to Caserta railway.

chapters.title: Mild valleys, colder heights
paras: Sheltered, well-exposed valley floors are mild, with rain of around 1000 mm a year. Higher up, winters are colder and summers moderately warm. Rain there can reach 1400 mm a year.
Dry spells last up to 2 months, from mid-June to mid-August, at lower altitude. They shrink to a minimum higher up. Rain peaks in autumn, and sometimes again in spring.
Air moves well near the ground across the zone. That gives the vines enough ventilation, which favours their growth and the health of the crop.

chapters.title: Soft rock, fine soils
paras: The soils are typical Regosols. Underneath lies mostly soft rock. It is sandstone and clay, or calcarenite, a limestone made of sand-sized grains. Scaly clays come in brick-red, green and grey. Limestone and dolomite also underlie some soils. Quaternary volcanic and other loose deposits blanket almost all the hills and fill the hollows.
Fine particles dominate, so the soils generally hold plenty of water. Calcium carbonate is normally present. The topsoil is generally shallow, and a slow-draining layer often lies just below it.

chapters.title: Aglianico, aged before it is sold
paras: Wines must be at least 85% Aglianico. The rest can come from other non-aromatic black grapes suited to the province of Benevento, up to 15%. Aglianico now covers over 50% of the registered vineyard area.
The name covers a red and a rosé. The red also comes as a riserva. The red is dry and full-bodied, ruby turning garnet with age. It must age at least 2 years from 1 November of the harvest year.

The riserva is an intense garnet, dry and full-bodied. It needs at least 3 years of ageing, with at least 12 months in wooden barrels and 6 months in bottle. New vineyards cannot make it before their fifth year.

The rosé, called rosato, is pink. It smells delicate and fruity, and tastes dry and fresh. It cannot be sold before 1 March of the year after the harvest. Any of the wines kept in wood may show a slight hint of it.
